newsitem.title: USA: 3Com counters Intel, shaves price. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]
newsitem.headline: 3Com counters Intel, shaves price. [CORRECTED 16:45 GMT]

text.p: A senior executive of 3Com Corp. said the company will respond to Intel Corp.'s latest networking products by cutting prices, but recent sales figures suggest Intel's actions may actually benefit 3Com.
Doug Spreng (corrects surname), executive vice president of interface products at Santa Clara, Calif.-based 3Com, said on Monday that the price decreases would not be material to 3Com earnings.

"This will have a negligible impact on our margins," he said in an interview. "This was not a shock for us. We had a cost reduction coming anyway. It's just not material. It won't change our financial model."
The executive also said that after Intel slashed certain network adapter prices in February, 3Com sales figures indicate its own products gained market share.
Spreng said 3Com, the market leader in networking products for desktop connectivity and workgroup settings, would use a similar strategy this time around.
"We'll be modifying two product prices actually in response to Intel," he told Reuters in an interview.

"Number one's going to be our Hub 100, which is our Fast Ethernet hub, and that'll end up about 10 percent above them in terms of price per port because we're worth more," he said. "We're the Loreal of the industry."

"The other one is we have a 10/100 product as well that's very similar to theirs and that one will also be priced accordingly," he said. "We believe we can gain that premium because we're shipping today, we don't have to prove anything and we can offer other value to customers."

Intel said Monday it was introducing a hub -- networking gear which connects computers together -- that could operate at 10 or 100 megabits per second at prices as low as $99 per port, a savings over existing hub products.
The 3Com executive said the Intel announcements had forced 3Com to advance the timetable of a price cut planned for the June time frame to this month instead.
"Two months doesn't make a huge amount of difference," he said. "They're marginalizing the weaker players here."
Spreng did not reveal specific details of the size of the new 3Com price cuts.

Intel also said it has developed a single-chip network connection device that could be installed directly on a motherboard. Since last autumn 3Com said it has been selling a motherboard product to Dell Computer.
Investors responded to the Intel news by dragging 3Com stock to a new year low, less than one third its 52-week peak of 81-3/8. 3Com shares closed down 2-7/8 at 26-3/8.

Spreng said the last Intel announcement to rock 3Com shares, its mid-February statement it was cutting adapter prices by nearly 40 percent, had caused it to drop prices too, but not to as low as Intel's products.
He said sales of its competing products rose 64 percent in the three months through the end of February, with the largest number of shipments coming in February.
Sales through the channel in the U.S. market are up nearly 50 percent on a unit basis in March, he said.

"We know the market's not growing at that rate, so we must be gaining market share at a tremendous rate," he said. "Just dropping prices is not going to ensure that they (Intel) are going to get market share."
